protocol: 32 original documents, 16 graded queries, K=5, all queries embedded anew; no server inference

documents.title: Browser inference
documents.text: Browser inference executes a neural network on the user's own device. Text is encoded locally without sending it to a cloud inference service. A model may be downloaded once and cached for later offline use.

documents.title: WebGPU acceleration
documents.text: WebGPU exposes the device GPU for browser computation. An embedding application should request a GPU adapter and explicitly select the webgpu execution provider. FP16 operations require the shader-f16 adapter feature.

documents.title: WASM fallback
documents.text: When no GPU adapter is available, an embedding application can use WebAssembly on the CPU. The interface should clearly show WASM as the active inference backend. INT8 models reduce download and memory cost.

documents.title: Quantization
documents.text: INT8 quantization stores many model weights as eight-bit integers instead of 32-bit floats. FP16 stores weights as 16-bit floats. Measure the actual model file sizes and validate retrieval quality after compression.

documents.title: Batch inference
documents.text: Embedding several texts in one inference call improves throughput by sharing runtime overhead. Similar-length texts can be grouped to reduce padding. Batch size should be bounded to keep memory use manageable.

documents.title: Worker responsiveness
documents.text: A Web Worker keeps tokenization and model inference off the browser's main UI thread. Progress messages let the page stay responsive while documents are being encoded. The worker can reuse a warm model session.

documents.title: Vector normalization
documents.text: A sentence embedding maps text to a fixed-size numerical vector. Mean pooling combines token representations. L2 normalization makes cosine similarity convenient for semantic retrieval across different document lengths.

documents.title: Semantic search
documents.text: Semantic search retrieves documents by meaning using embedding similarity. It can find a passage even when the query uses different words. A vector index such as HNSW makes approximate nearest-neighbor search efficient.

documents.title: Full-text search
documents.text: Full-text search tokenizes document text and ranks keyword matches. It is useful for exact product names, technical identifiers, and rare terms. An analyzer determines how words and language-specific tokens are indexed.

documents.title: Database hybrid search
documents.text: Hybrid retrieval combines lexical full-text matching with semantic vector search. In seekdb, DBMS_HYBRID_SEARCH builds a database query that can use reciprocal rank fusion. The browser must not merge two independent result lists as a replacement.

documents.title: Reciprocal rank fusion
documents.text: Reciprocal rank fusion combines rankings using the reciprocal of each rank plus a constant. It avoids comparing incompatible keyword and vector scores directly. A rank window limits how many candidates contribute.

documents.title: Index refresh
documents.text: After a batch of document writes, explicitly refresh seekdb indexes before declaring the import searchable. Refresh once per import instead of after every document to reduce overhead. Report refresh latency separately from write latency.

documents.title: Incremental imports
documents.text: Incremental imports add new document chunks without rebuilding the entire knowledge base. Stable content-derived IDs make importing the same file twice idempotent. A knowledge-base revision tracks whether the newest writes have been indexed.

documents.title: Collection isolation
documents.text: Each knowledge base should use its own collection. Save the selected collection across browser reloads. A search response from a previously selected collection must not overwrite the results of the current collection.

documents.title: Chunking documents
documents.text: Long documents are split into bounded overlapping chunks before embedding. Chunk metadata records the source filename and position. Preserving sentence boundaries makes displayed evidence easier to understand.

documents.title: Retrieval evaluation
documents.text: Recall at K measures the fraction of relevant documents found in the first K results. nDCG at K also accounts for ranking order and graded relevance. Use identical documents and queries to compare quantized and full-precision models.

documents.title: Latency measurement
documents.text: Measure model loading, document encoding, database writes, index refresh, query encoding, and retrieval separately. End-to-end query latency starts when the user submits the query and ends when results can be displayed. Report medians across repeated requests.

documents.title: Cold and warm runs
documents.text: The first browser request includes model file transfer, session creation, and runtime initialization. Later requests can reuse downloaded weights and a warm inference session. Report first-load and warm-request timings separately.

documents.title: Model identity
documents.text: Pin the embedding model repository and revision. Document vectors and query vectors must use the same model family, dimension, pooling, and normalization. Switching to a different model requires re-embedding stored documents.

documents.title: Browser privacy
documents.text: Local inference prevents document text from being sent to a remote AI provider. A local database still stores documents and vectors, so the application should state where storage resides. Network audits can verify that model inference never calls a cloud API.

documents.title: Parameter binding
documents.text: Database applications should bind SQL values instead of concatenating untrusted user input. Restrict generated collection identifiers to a safe format. Keep database credentials on the server rather than exposing them in browser JavaScript.

documents.title: Recovering an import
documents.text: If a write batch fails, mark the knowledge base as needing refresh and display the error. Preserve successfully stored chunks. A retry can upsert stable document IDs and then refresh indexes to restore a consistent searchable state.

documents.title: Cache management
documents.text: Browser caches avoid downloading model weights on every visit. Cache keys should include a pinned model revision to prevent stale artifacts from being mixed with new tokenizers. Clearing the browser cache makes a fresh download experiment reproducible.

documents.title: Reproducible experiments
documents.text: A reproducible performance experiment records device, browser version, model precision, backend, batch size, corpus, query set, and database configuration. Save all raw observations and report medians rather than selecting the fastest run.

documents.title: Database backups
documents.text: A database backup preserves stored records for recovery after disk failure. Restore tests verify that backups can be read. Backup retention policies are separate from browser model caching and vector index refresh.

documents.title: Image compression
documents.text: Image compression reduces the bytes needed to store photographs. JPEG uses lossy frequency transforms, while PNG supports lossless compression. Image file compression is different from quantizing neural network weights.

documents.title: GPU rendering
documents.text: A graphics pipeline turns geometry into pixels using vertex and fragment shaders. Rendering smooth animations is a graphics workload. Machine-learning compute kernels instead transform numerical tensors.

documents.title: Browser sessions
documents.text: A browser session may preserve UI preferences in localStorage. A knowledge-base identifier can be restored after page reload. Storage in localStorage must not substitute for seekdb document and vector storage.

documents.title: Sorting results
documents.text: A search interface presents evidence in the order returned by the database. Each result includes original text and source metadata. Scores from a rank-fusion query should not be mislabeled as cosine distances.

documents.title: CPU parallelism
documents.text: WASM threads can speed CPU inference when the page is cross-origin isolated. COOP and COEP headers enable SharedArrayBuffer in compatible browsers. Thread count should be recorded because it affects fair performance comparisons.

documents.title: ONNX portability
documents.text: ONNX is a model interchange format. ONNX Runtime Web executes exported networks in browsers using WebGPU or WASM providers. Exported operator support must be checked on both backends before shipping an application.

documents.title: Content versions
documents.text: Content-addressed chunk IDs distinguish changed file versions while deduplicating identical imports. The displayed source and chunk position help users identify the imported evidence. Separate collections provide stronger isolation between projects.
